author: Jack Whitmore
title: Trump Signs Iran Deal During Dinner at Versailles, Geneva Ceremony Cancelled
text:
President Trump signed the US-Iran memorandum of understanding Wednesday over dinner at the Palace of Versailles in France.
With his signature sealing the deal, the planned Geneva ceremony has been canceled.
A Candlelit Signing Video of the signing shows Trump autographing the deal with his signature black marker.
French President Macron and Secretary of State Marco Rubio sat at his side at the candlelit table.
Dinner guests applauded as Trump signed the document.
He was seen giving out the markers as mementos, as he often does at White House events.
“A pretty key moment in history we are sharing together,” Rubio said.
The agreement would end the three-month war against Iran and begin 60 days of nuclear talks.
Trump Seals the Deal Trump had witnessed Vice President JD Vance sign the document electronically on Sunday.
“On Sunday, the MOU was signed digitally by Vice President Vance and [Iranian Parliament] Speaker [Mohammad-Bagher] Ghalibaf and witnessed by President Trump,” a senior US official said.
“Now, it has been signed by President Trump and President Pezeshkian,” the official added.
US officials previously said Trump also electronically signed the document on Sunday.
Wednesday marked his turn to physically seal the agreement.
The signature lifted the US blockade on Iranian ports.
Geneva Ceremony Scrapped The original plan called for an in-person signing in Switzerland on Friday.
Vance — and potentially Trump — were to sign alongside senior Iranian officials.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said that ceremony has been canceled.
“The memorandum has been signed digitally and no signing ceremony will be held in Switzerland,” Baghaei said.
“The text of the Iran-U.S. memorandum is now officially finalized, because both sides have signed it,” he added.
Negotiating teams are still expected in Geneva, however.
Iran Locks In Its Signature Baghaei said the president of Iran would also sign Wednesday.
After that, he warned, “violating it will carry a higher cost.”
A senior US official telegraphed earlier that the Switzerland event was in doubt.
Masoud Pezeshkian
The official said signing could occur “remotely” and chalked up the change to Iranian “politics.”
President Pezeshkian signed for the Iranian side.
The dual signatures finalized the framework.
What Comes Next The key question now is whether Iran will make concessions in nuclear negotiations.
US officials want enough movement to warrant a final deal.
If Iran fails to do so, the US warned it would strengthen economic punishments.
It could also potentially re-establish the blockade on Iranian ports.
That blockade is now lifted with the president’s signature.
The next 60 days will test whether the framework holds.
summary: President Trump signed the US-Iran memorandum of understanding Wednesday over dinner at the Palace of Versailles in France. Video of the signing shows Trump autographing the deal with his signature black marker. French President Macron and Secretary of State Marco Rubio sat at his side at the candlelit table. Trump had witnessed Vice President JD Vance sign the document electronically on Sunday. After that, he warned, “violating it will carry a higher cost.” A senior US official telegraphed earlier that the Switzerland event was in doubt.
